What I don't understand about the new tournament rules is the happiness
with which the NCL camp received the increase in the limit on the
Restricted cards. I didn't think the DC tourney rules used the
much-touted "Golden Tenets" (no repeat actions, no vote pushing). Assuming
they don't (esp. since the Golden Tenet about vote pushing expressly
breaks the new V:TES rules on voting), how are they limiting degenerate
decks? A 6 card limit is not a limit at all (most NL decks I have seen
rely on maybe 7 or 8 copies of the "main" cards in the deck...big
difference). I'd rather use NL rules with a limited list (or NL
with the Golden Tenets) than no limits
at all. Wierd how NCL proponents seem to be so prejudiced against CL
that they are willing to let the game remain broken in tournaments to
avoid a card limit...

If I'm wrong about the DC using the "Golden Tenets", please let me know.
I am not really trempted to play a broken game in a tournament.

Messages.Author: Jonathan G. Sushinsky
Messages.Body:
>>Restricted cards. I didn't think the DC tourney rules used the
>>much-touted "Golden Tenets" (no repeat actions, no vote pushing). Assuming
>>they don't (esp. since the Golden Tenet about vote pushing expressly
>>breaks the new V:TES rules on voting), how are they limiting degenerate

What are the new V:TES rules for voting. I remember vote pushing as
being limited by the rules in the first place. I think (not sure
this is just how I have played)that the Jyhad rules limited vote pushing
by not allowing you to replace "thrown in votes" until the political
action was completed.

For example I have 4 KRCs in my hand and no other political cards. I
call KRC that is not blocked. That card is replaced, but I don't get
another political card. So the most votes I can then throw in are my
other three KRCs, since they cannot be replaced immediately.

In this situation vote pushing is limited to eight votes at the most
(if you don't count action modifiers and reactions:Bewitching Oration,
Dread Gaze) and I don't know anyone who would want to have a hand with
just political cards so in practice vote pushing is limited.

Anyway I don't have a rule book handy at the moment so this could just be
a rule that my group made up and I never thought to challenge. Any
thoughts or corrections are always welcome.

jon

don't believe that my play group is going to adopt the tourney rules.

Okay, for those of you who missed this the first time it ws posted, here
is my Brujah Cel/Pot Rush deck. It's based (though it's been modified to
suit my taste) on a deck posted by James McClure (thanks James). It
works pretty well for me, and though this started as an experiment, I've
found that I really like playing this deck:

Crypt (All Brujah):

Constanza Vinti
Donal O'Connor
Rake
Bianca
Anvil
Black Cat
Volker
Yuri
Uma
Dre
Lupo
Angel
Nik
--------------
13 Vamps (my personal choice for vamp number); average capacity--4.5

(I have separated the cards in the Library by rarity, because that's how
James' was divided up; I believe I have all the rarities right)

Rares
-----
2 Immortal Grapples
2 Fists of Death (just traded for 2 more, and thinking about putting them in)

Fragment of the Book of Nod

Giant's Blood
The Knights
The Slashers
Sengir Dagger
4 Pulled Fangs

13 Rares (Auspicious?)

Uncommons
---------
4 Torn Signposts
3 Second Traditions
4 Tastes of Vitae
3 Bloodhunts
2 Sport Bikes
2 Bastard Swords
2 Archon Investigations (just the threat of these slows down the bleeding...)
Major Boon
Mob Connections
Warzone Hunting Ground
KRCG News Radio
2 Malk Dementia
Information Highway

27 Uncommons

Commons
-------
4 Haven Uncovered
4 Bum's Rush
2 Trap
Elder Intervention
4 Wakes w/Evening Freshness
2 Lucky Blow
2 Short Term Investment
3 Blood Doll
Potence
Celerity
4 Undead Strength
2 Burning Wrath
4 Acrobatics
4 Blur
4 Sideslip
2 Nimble Feet
2 Vampiric Speed
4 Flash

50 Commons

90 Cards Total

With 4 different (all reasonably-priced) Princes in the Crypt, the deck
is reasonably certain to be able to use all of the Prince-specific cards
in the Library (Bloodhunts, 2nd Traditions), though it can win without
getting any of the Princes out. The Princes also help in PA's, of
course. With an average of (approx.) 4.5 capacity in the Crypt, the
number of vamps out is similar to other (non-weenie-horde) decks.
Comments are welcome.

> Uma Dre
> Lupo Angel
> Nik 13 Vamps (my personal choice for vamp number); average capacity--4.5

Assuming you go fourth, you will be on the third turn before a prince
reliably comes up, and the fourth turn before you can use bloodhunts.

BLOOD HELPERS

> 3 Blood Doll

> Giant's Blood
> Warzone Hunting Ground

SPEED and EFFICIENCY

> Potence
> Celerity

> The Knights
> The Slashers
> Sengir Dagger

> 2 Bastard Swords

> 2 Malk Dementia
> Information Highway

Again, good choices except for the Knights/Slashers/Swords. They are
slow to equip and either not much use for blocking a Sneaking Vampire,
cost pool, and your highly intensive combat deck doesn't need 1 more
damage. Another Sengir Dagger for instant torpor is much better. Add a
Barrens to get rid of hand jam. More blood suckers (Dolls, Taps,
whatever) and generic intercept (elder intervention will make this better).

> 90 Cards Total
>
> With 4 different (all reasonably-priced) Princes in the Crypt, the deck
> is reasonably certain to be able to use all of the Prince-specific
cards
> in the Library (Bloodhunts, 2nd Traditions), though it can win without
> getting any of the Princes out. The Princes also help in PA's, of
> course. With an average of (approx.) 4.5 capacity in the Crypt, the
> number of vamps out is similar to other (non-weenie-horde) decks.
> Comments are welcome.

I think you'd have a bit of trouble against a MS&B predator. Though you
may hold them off, I think you'd have a lot of difficulty in getting a VP
as well. I don't think you particularly need more combat cards, but some
of the drops I suggested might be best not replaced, to increase overall
tightness.

Replies welcome by email or post...

Messages.Author: Mark Havener
Messages.Body:
Okay, one more note on the 4CL Cel/Pot Rush deck that I have been
experimenting with (yes, the experiment continues! ;) ). To date, the
deck is 6 wins out of 8 games (in 3 of those games, including one
tonight, I was the only one who got VPs). The deck has been played in
games of from 3 to 6 players, in two different groups (mostly my usual
Tuesday night group though). All clans (including the two new ones)
have been represented in at least one game (played against a Giovani deck
tonight...TB...yuck! ;) ). The players have included the "core" members
of my Tuesday group, as well as "walk-ins", and of course, the members of
another group, so a wide variety of players has also been represented.
I'd consider myself a fairly good deck builder/player, but most of my
regular group is just as good, so there's not a real advantage there.

The deck is just good! And very fun to play too! I used to have a lot
of fun with my "Anson and (Brujah) Friends" deck, but this deck is just
as fun. It's as effective, if not more so, than my other deck. It's
become the main deck I play (started out as an experiment growing out of
a "CL/NCL discussion, but it's too fun now...I've always loved Brujah, of
course...).

I have to admit, I wasn't *sure* if Cel/Pot Rush was valid under 4CL, but
after trying out this deck (a modification of a NL deck posted by James
McClure), I am convinced that it IS a viable deckbuilding strategy. And
a pretty fun one too...

I have included the deck I am using at the bottom of this post, just in
case anyone missed the post AND re-post. Since no one commented on the
re-post...

-Elfholme

Messages.Author: Alec Habig
Messages.Body:
Looks good! It's good to see that this deck design works ok under 4CL, now you
can play a closer approximation to real Jyhad :)

I was looking at this deck trying to think of how it was different than a
similar deck under NL, to try and get a better feel for how the two games
differ.

First, I'd put in more Bum's Rush and Haven Uncovered - mostly Bum's Rush.
This deck doesn't have much intercept, and I'd rather take a bleed from it than
get into a fight, so its main means means of getting into combat are 4 BR, 4HU,
and 3 Bloodhunt (votes from a Prince/Justicar, not particularly reliable).
Enough combats for keeping your predator at bay and messing up your prey, but
not much more than that.

This makes me think that this deck is somewhat less effective than it's NL
brother would be - no great surprise there, that's a given by all parties in
this debate. However, it is still a "viable" deck, as Mark has proven by
winning with it. A question, though - what do you do to get in combat if the
other guys decide they don't want to block you? I could see this grinding to a
halt, and might suggest adding some things that make people come after you -
Powerbases, racks, blood puppy, Smiling Jack. Put in some Rampages, so they
have to choose between a coveted location and staying out of a fight.

The other difference I notices was the use of rares. I'm constructing a
similar NL deck, and don't have many (I've got : Pulled fangs, Giant's Blood,
Knights) of the rares needed by Mark's deck. However, I am comfortable with
most of the less rare (and expensive) replacement cards - Loyal Street Bump,
Stake, potence common strikes.

(speaking of which, I went to r.g.t-c.misc today looking for trades, and there
isn't much Jyhad action going on. My trade post looks pretty lonely after
killfiling non-Jyhad posts).

Anyway, congrats on solving a long standing puzzle.

--
